purpose: Publish every package whose current version is untagged (registry publish, git tag, GitHub release) either locally with `callisto release` or from CI through plan, artifact-manifest and execute, using the merged release PR's committed decision as the only release authority. Every effect is checked against the registry, Git remote or GitHub first, so a rerun finishes a partial release without repeating anything.
scope: Local `callisto release`, the hidden CI release subcommands, decision verification and source checks, operation order, registry publish and observation, reruns and receipts, tags and GitHub releases and assets, the managed release PR, `[release]` config, and release error codes.
non_goals: Forges other than GitHub, and publish targets other than crates.io-style Cargo registries, npm and PyPI.
Checking registry credentials before publishing; cargo, npm, twine and gh report their own auth failures.
A workspace lock file; re-observing Git state before every operation guards against concurrent changes.
Persisting execution state between runs; a rerun re-observes providers from scratch.
Apple code signing and notarization of product assets.

api_surface.name: callisto release
api_surface.description: Publishes every untagged package from the current checkout on any branch. With --dry-run it prints the plan and performs no effect.
error_conditions: Dirty worktree: E267.
Workspace needs the CI route: E239.
Invalid --package, or a snapshot version: E227, E102 or E169.
Missing or unsafe origin push URL: E132.

api_surface.name: callisto release plan (hidden)
api_surface.signature: callisto release plan [--source-root DIR] (--from-release-commit SHA --decision FILE | --package ECOSYSTEM/NAME...) [--orchestration-revision SHA --artifact-repository OWNER/REPO] --out FILE
api_surface.description: Writes a release plan file (JSON, schemaVersion 5) for a detached source checkout. With --from-release-commit it verifies the committed decision file. With --package it derives the roster from a fresh version plan.
error_conditions: --dry-run: E309.
Commit verification failure: E165.
[release] present without both orchestration flags: E231.

api_surface.name: callisto release build-python (hidden)
api_surface.signature: callisto release build-python [--source-root DIR] --intent FILE --artifact-dir DIR
api_surface.description: Builds the sdist and wheel of every Python publish in the plan into the directory, without registry credentials.
error_conditions: --dry-run: E309.
Plan publishes no Python package: E308.
A build with no wheel or no sdist: E306.

api_surface.name: callisto release package-cargo (hidden)
api_surface.description: Runs `cargo package --locked -p <crate>...` for every crate the plan publishes, one call per owning Cargo workspace and from that workspace's directory, without registry credentials.
error_conditions: --dry-run: E309.
Plan publishes no crate: E308.
A cargo package that fails: E164.

api_surface.name: callisto release pack-npm (hidden)
api_surface.signature: callisto release pack-npm [--source-root DIR] --intent FILE --artifact-dir DIR
api_surface.description: Packs every npm publish in the plan, platform packages included, into the directory with its workspace's package manager, without registry credentials. The package's `prepack` and `prepare` scripts run here.
error_conditions: --dry-run: E309.
Plan publishes no npm package: E308.
A pack that writes no tarball, or one not named for the package and version: E306.

api_surface.name: callisto release artifact-manifest (hidden)
api_surface.signature: callisto release artifact-manifest --intent FILE --artifact-dir DIR [--seal-python] [--seal-npm] --out FILE
api_surface.description: Hashes one regular file per declared artifact slot and writes the artifact manifest. With --seal-python it also records the name, size and sha256 of every built Python file of the plan, and with --seal-npm that of the tarball of every npm publish.
error_conditions: Plan declares no slots and neither --seal-python nor --seal-npm is given: E219.
--seal-python on a plan that publishes no Python package, or --seal-npm on one that publishes no npm package: E308.
--seal-npm with a tarball missing from the directory: E306.
Asset missing, a symlink or not a regular file: E221.

api_surface.name: callisto release execute (hidden)
api_surface.signature: callisto release execute [--source-root DIR] --intent FILE [--artifact-manifest FILE --artifact-dir DIR] --receipt FILE --orchestration-revision SHA
api_surface.description: Validates the plan file against a fresh derivation from the source checkout, runs every operation, and writes the receipt on full success.
error_conditions: --dry-run: E309.
Stale plan: E124.
Incomplete run: E172.

api_surface.name: callisto release inspect (hidden)
api_surface.description: Prints a plan, artifact manifest or receipt JSON document without recomputing it.

api_surface.name: callisto release-pr decide | verify | commit-plan
api_surface.signature: release-pr decide --snapshot FILE|JSON|- --repository OWNER/REPO --base-branch B --release-branch R; release-pr verify --decision X --snapshot X [--applied-head SHA]; release-pr commit-plan --base-commit SHA --message M [--out FILE]
api_surface.description: Decides noop, create or update for the managed release PR from a forge snapshot, re-verifies that snapshot, and builds the commit-API file changes from the staged Git index.

api_surface.name: callisto version --emit-decision
api_surface.description: Writes the release decision (package, target version, inclusion reasons) next to the manifest and changelog edits it applies.

api_surface.name: [release] in callisto.toml
api_surface.description: Declares the product package and the binary assets attached to its GitHub release, which goes to origin's GitHub repository unless forge-repository names it.
error_conditions: No target or [[release.artifact]], targets without asset-name or the reverse, a placeholder other than {target}, a target named by both targets and a [[release.artifact]] of the product, an unqualified package, an unsafe target or asset-name, a duplicate asset-name, or an unsupported profile: E197.
Neither forge-repository nor a GitHub origin when planning: E198.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `callisto release` selects every package that has a publish target other than `none` and whose current version has no matching tag, or has a tag on the current commit while any of its operations is not observed already satisfied. For each one it runs the registry publishes, creates the git tag, and creates the GitHub release when `github-release` is a target. A tag on another commit marks the version released without contacting any provider.

When no package qualifies, `callisto release` prints `Nothing to release.` (JSON: `{"nothingToRelease": true}`, plus a `diagnostics` array when there is pending version work), exits 0 and runs no command that publishes, pushes or creates anything.
`callisto release` runs on any branch, leaves HEAD on that branch, and records HEAD's commit as both `releaseSourceRevision` and `orchestrationRevision` in the receipt.

`callisto release --dry-run` prints a `Release plan:` header and each package as `<ecosystem/name> <version>` with its operations (a table on a colour terminal, indented lines otherwise) and performs no effect. This holds on a dirty worktree, without an `origin` remote, and in a workspace that needs the CI route. With `--format json` it prints the plan document, whose `digest` equals the receipt's `intentDigest` from a following `callisto release` on the same state; the document carries a sibling `diagnostics` array (e.g. an artifact owner selected without its product) when derivation raised any, and omits the field otherwise. `release plan`'s JSON output carries the same `diagnostics` array; the `--out` file it writes never does.

Without an `origin` push URL, or with one that is not a hosted remote (an `https://` or `ssh://git@` URL naming an owner and repository, or `git@host:owner/repo`), `--dry-run` prints one stderr note that names why `origin` cannot bind tags and says tag operations are unbound, and `callisto release` fails with E132 before any effect, without naming the `origin` value. While `callisto version` has pending work for a package the release would cover (changesets only, never commit inference; in a prerelease cycle, only notes not yet applied; publishable packages only, narrowed and group-expanded by `--package`), `--dry-run` also prints one stderr note to run it first, as does `callisto release` when there is nothing to release or the selection is refused as not a release (E169); `--format json --dry-run` also lists it in the report's `diagnostics`. When that check itself fails, one stderr note names the error code and points at `callisto status`, and the command's own result is unchanged. With neither `forge-repository` nor a GitHub `origin`, `--dry-run` still validates each artifact's owner (E179) and reports every configured asset as an `artifact-without-forge-destination` warning, a diagnostic with no error code, since the asset is bound to no destination.

A tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore` makes `callisto release` fail with E267 naming a clean worktree and the offending path, before any effect. Ignored files never count.
Repeated `--package <ecosystem/name>` limits the run to the named packages, every distribution of each, and every package that shares a `fixed` or `linked` group with one of them.

A `--package` value in colon form (`cargo:x`) fails with E316, any other malformed value with E227, and an unknown package with E102. A duplicate selection, a version whose release is complete, a package with no publish target, or a package whose current version is a `callisto snapshot` version fails with E169.

Suppose a selected package has a runtime, optional or peer dependency on a publishable workspace package whose current version is untagged, and that package is not selected. Planning fails with E169 ("select it too") before any effect. A dependency whose current version is already tagged need not be selected.

In a workspace with `[[release.artifact]]` slots or a napi/maturin platform package, `callisto release` fails with `E239` before any effect. The help names `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest` and `release execute`.

On success, text output is `Released N package(s)`, followed by `; receipt saved to <path>` when `--receipt` is given, and JSON output is the receipt. A receipt file is written only to the `--receipt` path, never into the checkout, and an unwritable `--receipt` path fails the run before any effect.

`--format json` output of `release`, `release --dry-run`, `release plan`, `release execute`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release pending` and `release build-python` goes through the same envelope every other command's JSON report uses: a top-level `schemaVersion`, `command` (the subcommand name) and `dryRun`, alongside that subcommand's own payload fields unchanged. The intent and artifact-manifest --out files, receipt --receipt file and version --emit-decision file use their durable document shape without command or dryRun wrapper fields. A failing command's `--format json` error, printed to stderr, carries the same `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun` as its success report, with the `error` object after them. Stderr holds that JSON and nothing else.

`release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path>` takes the package and version roster from the decision file committed in that commit. It does not re-run changeset, group, cascade or pre-release selection.

`release plan --from-release-commit` fails with E165 and writes no output file in any of these cases: HEAD is not the given commit; the commit neither adds nor modifies the decision file; the direct-child changeset `.md` files it deletes (nested Markdown files and `README.md` do not count) are not exactly the decision's `consumedChangesets`, or, for a decision older than that field, it deletes none; a claimed package's manifest does not change to its claimed version; a claimed package's changelog is unchanged; an unclaimed manifest version changes; a claimed package is not found; or the commit changes any path other than a manifest (`Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`) or lockfile (`Cargo.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock`, `bun.lockb`, `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `pdm.lock`) anywhere, a package's changelog, the decision file, a direct-child changeset, or the changesets directory's `pre.json`.

A committed decision file whose digest does not match its entries fails with E166. Each target version is parsed using the grammar of its package ecosystem; durable operation IDs, artifact slots and registry observations bound to an operation use that same grammar. Version values remain strings on the wire, and decision schema versions 1 and 2 are accepted; any other version fails with an error naming the version found.

An abbreviated or unknown `--from-release-commit` SHA, a non-40-hex `--orchestration-revision` for a source with `[release]`, or an `--intent` file with a different `schemaVersion` (`E215`, naming found and expected versions) fails before any output file is written or any effect runs.

`release plan` and `release execute` require the source checkout at a detached HEAD and fail with E170 otherwise. `callisto release` accepts an attached HEAD. Every route requires a complete, non-shallow SHA-1 repository and fails with E265 for a repository that is not SHA-1 and E266 for a shallow one.

`release execute` re-derives the plan from the source checkout and fails with E124 before any effect when the result differs from the `--intent` file. A change to the decision, source commit, manifests, config, registry binding or origin remote is enough.

Before each operation, the executor re-checks HEAD, worktree cleanliness and the `origin` push URL. A change stops the run before that operation's effect, with E124 for a moved HEAD or a changed `origin` push URL, E132 when `origin` has lost its push URL, and E267 for a dirty worktree.

`release plan` for a source with `[release]` requires `--orchestration-revision` and `--artifact-repository` (`E231`). For a source without `[release]` it ignores both flags, prints a notice, and plans zero artifact slots.

The GitHub destination is `[release].forge-repository` when set, else the `origin` GitHub repository. Planning rejects an `--artifact-repository` that differs from an explicit `forge-repository` (`E230`) or from the `origin` GitHub repository (E175). Execution rejects artifact slots that target another repository, and a `[release]` section with neither fails planning with E198.

A graph package has one tag, GitHub release draft and publish, however many ecosystems it publishes to. Its tag is created only after all selected registry publishes belonging to its canonical manifests succeed, in every ecosystem a dual Cargo and npm package publishes to, and its GitHub release draft only after its tag. A `[[release.artifact]]` slot's upload follows the product's draft and gates the product's publish even when a different selected package owns the asset, and the product's publish also waits for the tag of that package, which follows its registry publishes, so the release is published only after the draft, every upload and every publish behind them.

A selected package publishes after the selected packages it depends on through runtime, build, optional or dev edges, and waits for the dependency's distribution in the ecosystem of the declaring manifest, so a Cargo dependent follows a dual package's crate and an npm dependent follows its npm package. Only the dependent's distribution in that ecosystem waits: a dual dependent's Cargo-only dependency orders its crate, not its npm package, and the reverse; a dependency declared only by a manifest the package does not publish, such as a napi package's Cargo.toml, orders nothing, and so does a dependency's distribution in that ecosystem that the release does not publish. An npm dependent follows the dependency's publish command, not the registry showing the version. A dependency with no distribution in the declaring ecosystem is waited for in every ecosystem it publishes to. Cycles are found among the distributions the release publishes through exactly these waits: a dev edge between two distributions in the same cycle does not order them, a runtime, build or optional cycle fails with E104, and opposite edges between two packages in different ecosystems are not a cycle.

An npm package with attached platform packages publishes each platform package's tarball before the owner package's. Operations start one at a time and a failed publish command stops the run, so an owner package is never published after the command for one of its platform packages fails.

An npm registry publish, platform packages included, is issued without waiting for the registry to show the version, and stays unconfirmed. Another npm publish may then start, but no tag, GitHub release draft, upload or publication does until the registry has shown the version of every publish behind it. When no operation can start, Callisto looks at every unconfirmed publish together and waits between looks, 15 s, 45 s, 2 minutes, then 3 minute steps, for as long as the longest `confirm-timeout` among them (default 6 minutes), so the wait is the slowest registry's and not the sum. That window opens when the first of the publishes is issued and runs on the clock, so the time spent looking counts, and a publish that is shown along the way does not start it again or restart the 15 s, 45 s, 2 minute schedule. A look's own retries, including a registry's `Retry-After`, wait no longer in total than the window has left, and a look made with none left tries once. A publish still not shown then fails the run with E157, naming the first, and no receipt is written; a rerun adopts every version already published. Cargo and PyPI publishes are confirmed as they are published.

Cargo publish runs `cargo publish --manifest-path <pkg>/Cargo.toml --locked` from the directory of the Cargo workspace that governs the package, adding `--registry <key>` for registries other than crates.io, and `--no-verify` when `release execute` publishes, because a credential-free job already compiled every crate of the release; a local `callisto release` keeps cargo's verification. It runs only after the on-disk version (resolving `version.workspace = true`) equals the planned version and fails with an on-disk version drift error otherwise.

npm publish packs with the tool of the workspace that owns the package, then publishes the tarball with `npm`. The owner is the nearest directory at or above the package whose `package.json` declares `workspaces` or whose `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has a `packages` list, else for a package no workspace declares the nearest directory with a lockfile, else the root; a lockfile beside a package never moves it out of a declared workspace. The `npm view` observation and the publish run in that same directory, so one `.npmrc` governs what is looked for and what is published. A marker that cannot be inspected is an error, not `npm`. A `pnpm-workspace.yaml` alone, without a lockfile, selects pnpm. The pack runs in the package directory without registry credentials: `pnpm pack --pack-destination <dir>`, `yarn pack --out <dir>/package.tgz`, `bun pm pack --destination <dir>`, and otherwise `npm pack --pack-destination <dir>`; a platform package is always packed with `npm`. The pack must leave exactly one tarball whose `package.json` names the package and version, or the run fails with E306. It is staged as `<flattened name>-<version>.tgz`, and a scoped package carries a digest of its full name in that name, so `@acme/lib` and `acme-lib` at one version stay two files. The publish is `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`, so only `prepack` and `prepare` run, in the pack, and `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` do not run. It appends `--tag <label>` for prerelease versions, where the label is the lowercase letters that start the first prerelease identifier (`1.0.0-beta.2` publishes under `beta`), or `next` when there are none or the word is `latest`, and `--access` and `--registry` when set. A stable version takes the registry default tag.

A scoped npm package (`@scope/name`) with no configured access publishes with `--access public`. A configured access value always wins, and an unscoped package with no configured access gets no `--access` flag.

PyPI publish builds with `python3 -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir <temporary directory>` in the package directory, falling back to `python` and failing with E170 when neither is on PATH, and fails with E306 when the build produced no wheel or no sdist for the version. It then runs `twine upload` naming only the built files the index lacks, with `--repository-url` for a configured upload endpoint (a registry's `publish-url`, else its `url`) and never `--skip-existing`. One build serves the preflight and the publish of a run. Every build runs with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set to the release commit's committer time. `release build-python` runs the same build for each Python publish of a plan into `--artifact-dir`.

An npm publish of a run whose artifact manifest seals the package's tarball publishes that file and packs nothing: the manifest records the tarball's name, size and sha256 (`release pack-npm`, then `release artifact-manifest --seal-npm`), `release execute` verifies the bytes before any effect and the publish checks them again just before it runs, and a mismatch fails with E139. A manifest that seals a Python or npm publish's files seals every publish of that ecosystem in the plan, or none. `release execute` with an npm or PyPI publish in the plan and no manifest, or a manifest that does not seal one of those publishes, fails with E306 when the manifest is verified, before any effect, and again before the publish command, so a package's scripts and build backend never run beside registry credentials. Only the local `callisto release`, which has no manifest, packs in place: the tarball is packed in a temporary directory with registry credentials withheld from the pack, then published the same way.

A `publishConfig.registry` in package.json that does not match the `url` of an npm-kind `[registries]` entry fails with E120. A registry URL that is not `https`, or has userinfo, a query or a fragment, fails with E126. An `origin` push URL that is not HTTPS or `git@` SSH, or that carries credentials, fails with E132, which never names the value. All three fail before any effect.

Cargo observation runs `cargo --config net.retry=0 info NAME@VERSION --registry <name>` from the directory of the Cargo workspace that governs the package, passing `crates-io` for the default and the registry's own name for a `kind = "cargo"` registry named in `publish-to`, which `cargo publish` receives as `--registry <name>` too. Exit 0 with a matching `version:` line means present, exit 101 with ``could not find `NAME@VERSION` `` means absent, and anything else is indeterminate.

npm observation runs `npm view NAME@VERSION --json --fetch-retries=0`, with `--registry` when configured. Exit 0 with output means present. A failure whose npm error code is E404, read from the JSON error body on stdout or, when stdout is empty, from the `code` line on stderr (other output is indeterminate), means absent. Exit 0 with no output, and any other failure, leave the observation indeterminate and are never read as absence.

PyPI observation fetches `<index>/<normalized-name>/` (the registry's `url`, default `https://pypi.org/simple`; never its `publish-url`) with `curl` and `Accept: application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json`. In a 200 JSON body, any matching yanked file means absent; otherwise at least one matching non-yanked file means present. That version-level read serves every use outside an effect. Before a PyPI effect, `release execute` proceeds without a build when the index has no file of the version. Otherwise it builds, and treats the release as already satisfied only when every built file is on the index by filename and not yanked. A built file the index holds yanked is a remote conflict, and a file the index holds that the build did not produce is reported with a warning and not checked. After an upload, confirmation waits for every built file to be visible, and a file this run uploaded must carry the sha256 the index serves for it, or the run fails with E307. A file from an earlier attempt is matched by name, not by digest, unless the artifact manifest seals the release's files: then the run builds nothing, uploads those exact files, compares the sha256 of every file the index holds under a sealed name, and fails with E307 before any upload when one differs. A 404 or no matching file means absent, and a non-JSON body or other non-retryable status is indeterminate. Transient HTTP statuses use the observation retry policy.

After a publish command reports success, or says the version already exists, Callisto re-observes the registry and treats "absent" or an unreachable registry as not yet propagated, waiting within the registry's confirmation window: `confirm-timeout` on its `[registries]` entry (1 s to 1 h, written as `90s`, `6m` or `1h`), else 6 minutes for npm and PyPI and 2 minutes for Cargo. Looks are spaced 15 s, 45 s, 2 minutes, then 3 minutes apart, or by the registry's `Retry-After`; no wait runs past the window. A publish whose version the registry never shows in that window fails with E157, and no receipt is written.

Read-only observations before an effect (registry query, GitHub release lookup, `git ls-remote`) run at most 5 attempts with exponential backoff from 2 s, capped at 300 s. HTTP 429, 5xx, rate-limited 403 and failed commands are retried, and an observation still indeterminate fails with E176 before that operation's effect.

A publish command that fails fails the run with E163. For an auth failure the error carries the command's standard error; for a rate limit it carries the wait the tool asked for and no command output; for any other failure it carries the last 8 lines of standard output followed by standard error. A publish run echoes its standard error to the live log, and npm and PyPI publishes also echo standard output; `cargo publish` standard output is not echoed. A failing git or gh effect command fails with E164. No effect command is re-issued automatically. Tool output shown in these errors, in the live stderr echo and in JSON errors has credentials masked as `[REDACTED]`: the values of the known credential variables, of `CARGO_REGISTRIES_*_TOKEN`, and of any variable named `*_TOKEN`, `*_SECRET` or `*_PASSWORD` whose value is at least 8 characters, URL userinfo, `npm_`, `ghp_`-family, `github_pat_` and `pypi-` tokens of at least 20 characters after the prefix, `Bearer` values of at least 16 characters, and `.npmrc` `_authToken`, `_auth` and `_password` values.

A `pypi` `[registries]` entry may set `publish-url`, the endpoint Twine uploads to when the index at `url` is not also the upload route. Both endpoints follow the registry URL rules of REL-PUB-05 and both enter the registry binding, so changing either makes an earlier intent stale. A package-level `publish-to` index names both routes and overrides the entry's `publish-url`. A `publish-url` on a registry that is not `pypi` is rejected when the configuration loads.

A registry entry may set `publish-timeout`, the longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run, as a whole number with `s`, `m` or `h` from 1 s to 1 h; the default is 15 minutes. A command that runs longer is stopped and fails with E025. The value does not enter the registry binding, so changing it does not make an earlier intent stale. A value outside that form or range is rejected when the configuration loads.

When a Cargo or npm registry publish is adopted because the exact version is already published, and the registry entry names a repository whose host, owner and name differ from the `origin` remote's (compared case-insensitively, ignoring `.git`, `git+` and URL form), Callisto prints a warning on stderr naming both repositories. The run still adopts the version. No warning is printed when the registry names no repository, when either value cannot be read as a repository, or when they match. PyPI is not checked. When the package has no tag in this repository (a first release) and the registry holds the version under a differing repository, `release` and `release --dry-run` fail with E322 before anything else, because the version is another project's; tagging the commit that set the version by hand makes the package no longer a first release.

`crates-io` (kind `cargo`), `npm` and `pypi` are predeclared registries; a `[registries.<name>]` entry of the same name configures one and may leave `kind` out, and giving it another `kind` fails config loading with E334. Any other entry must set `kind` to `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`, or config loading fails with E321. A name that is not letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starts with `-`, is `github-release` or `none`, or is `cratesIo` fails config loading with E325; the `cratesIo` message names `[registries.crates-io]`.

A package this repository has never tagged that publishes to crates.io must set `description` and either `license` or `license-file` in its `Cargo.toml`, directly or from `[workspace.package]`; an empty value counts as unset. Otherwise `release` and `release --dry-run` stop with E323 naming the package and the missing field, before any publish, tag or push.

Every Callisto-launched child other than Cargo has `CARGO_REGISTRIES_*_TOKEN` variables removed, matched without case sensitivity, whether inherited or supplied to a publisher subprocess. This covers ordinary, timeout, filtered, stdin, quiet and publisher routes. Cargo keeps named registry tokens for its native authentication.

A registry destination in `callisto.toml` is honored or refused, never ignored. A `url` on a `cargo` registry fails config loading with E336, because cargo takes its URL from `.cargo/config.toml`. A `publish-to` entry that is not `github-release`, `none`, `crates-io`, `npm`, `pypi` or the name of a `cargo` registry fails config loading with E330. An npm registry `url` is passed to the publish as `--registry <url>` whichever package manager packed the tarball. A registry that only yarn or bun reads, `npmPublishRegistry` or `npmRegistryServer` in the owning workspace's `.yarnrc.yml` (at the top level or under `npmScopes`) or a registry in its `bunfig.toml`, fails with E168 naming the file and key when the plan is derived, on the local route too and before any effect, because `npm publish <tarball>` does not read it; `publishConfig.registry` and `.npmrc` are honored.

An operation whose result is already present and identical is recorded as already satisfied, and its effect is not repeated. For a registry version, stderr shows `warning: <package> <version> is already published; skipping`. During `release execute`, a Python release is satisfied only when every file its build produces is on the index, so a rerun after a partial upload uploads only the missing files. The check that finds a tagged package still to finish reads the version-level answer and does not build.

After a run fails partway, rerunning the same command with no state file from the failed run performs only the missing operations and writes a receipt. A local annotated tag on the expected commit that is missing on the remote is pushed before the receipt is written, regardless of its annotation text. `Nothing to release.` is reported only when every operation of every package tagged on the current commit is observed already satisfied. A failure to read the local tag state other than the tag being missing stops the run with an error before any effect.

Any of these fails with E167 and is never adopted: a local or remote tag on another commit, a lightweight tag, a GitHub release with a different prerelease flag, an asset of the same name with a different size or sha256, or two assets with the same name. A tag's identity is its target commit plus being annotated; annotation text is never compared.

A receipt is written only when every operation ends `published` or `alreadySatisfied`, and otherwise the run exits 1 with no receipt file (E172 when operations remain incomplete). The receipt records `intentDigest`, the envelope (`orchestrationRevision`, `releaseSourceRevision`, intent and artifact-manifest digests), and each operation's outcome and provider evidence.

`workflow_dispatch` with `release_source_sha` releases that commit using the current workflow run's commit as the orchestration revision. The SHA must be 40 lowercase hex characters, resolve to that same commit, lie on the triggering `main` commit's history, and equal the exact merge commit of one GitHub-verified PR merged into `main` from `callisto/version-packages` or `callisto/version-packages--<40-hex>` in the same repository. An invalid explicit source fails the candidate job without planning or updating the release PR. A valid recovery run skips `verify`, uses `recovery-checks`, and does not update the release PR before execution.
A tag push that GitHub refuses because the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip fails with E180, naming the tag and target commit.

A local `callisto release` refuses with E320, before any effect, when the registry already holds a version it would release and the package's files differ from the commit that set that version, or no commit on the first-parent history sets it. The version is read from the package manifest or, for a Cargo package that inherits it, from the workspace manifest; files are compared by content, so a reverted change and a change made inside a merge commit count. The error names the version commit; checking it out and running `callisto release` again adopts the published version and tags that commit. A registry that cannot be read stops the release before any effect. A package whose manifest is not committed is not checked here; the clean-tree rule covers it. A package whose files match that commit, or whose version the registry does not yet hold, is unaffected.

`callisto release` and `callisto release --dry-run` print a warning on stderr for each package's last tag that exists in the repository but not on `origin` (one `git ls-remote` for all of them), saying its release may not have finished. The warning does not change the plan or the exit status, and nothing is printed when there is no `origin`, no tag, or the remote cannot be read.

On a main push or manual dispatch without an explicit source, the repository's release workflow builds Callisto and takes the first release from `callisto release pending` as the source; with none pending, it examines the triggering commit. It rejects a selected source that is not an ancestor of the triggering main commit or is not the exact merge commit of exactly one GitHub-verified managed PR, rather than moving on to a newer release PR. Nothing is recorded on the PR; the committed decision and provider observations remain authoritative.

After `execute` succeeds, including receipt upload, the workflow dispatches the oldest unfinished release other than the one just executed, by full merge SHA; when none remains, it refreshes the managed release PR for changesets now on main. A failed execution leaves the release unfinished and selected again. A failed dispatch fails the drain job and does not refresh the release PR. The drain job receives no registry secrets.

`callisto release pending` lists, oldest first, the merged release commits whose release did not finish, from the last `--limit` commits (default 10) on HEAD's first-parent line that wrote the committed decision file (`--decision`, default `.callisto/release-decision.json`). A release is finished when every package in that commit's decision that has a publish target has a tag for its version, and every such package released to GitHub has a published (not draft) release; one that cannot be read counts as unfinished. A package missing from the current workspace, or without a publish target, is skipped; with neither `forge-repository` nor a GitHub `origin` the GitHub release check is skipped; a decision that cannot be decoded is an error. The scan stops at the newest finished release, since releases are sequential. With `--from <sha>` only that release commit and newer ones count, and a SHA that is not a release commit on the branch is an error. The command lists the commit, its packages and versions, and what is missing, in text or in JSON under `pending`, inside the same `schemaVersion`, `command` (`release pending`) and `dryRun` envelope as every other report; it publishes nothing and exits 0 when there are none.
Every package with a publish target gets an annotated, unsigned tag named by its tag template, with message `Release <tag>`, on the source commit, pushed to the `origin` push URL.

A package that targets `github-release` gets `gh release create <tag> --repo <owner/repo> --verify-tag --draft`, adding `--prerelease` for prerelease versions. After all its assets upload, the release is published with `gh release edit <tag> --draft=false`.

Release notes are the body of the package CHANGELOG section for the version, passed with `--notes-file`. For a package in a fixed group, the entries that the group's other members recorded for the same version follow, each as ``- `<ecosystem/name>`: <entry>``; the package's own section is kept whole (headings and paragraphs included), and its group boilerplate lines are dropped only when another member adds entries, an entry is left out when its text is identical to one the notes already hold, and a member without a changelog section adds nothing. With no changelog configured, a missing file, or a missing or empty section, Callisto passes `--generate-notes` and prints `notes: using generated notes (<reason>) for <package>` to stderr. A changelog that exists but cannot be read (a permission error, a directory, bytes that are not UTF-8) fails release planning with E125 naming the file, because generated notes would silently replace what the release PR reviewed.

Each artifact (a `[[release.artifact]]` or a `[release] targets` expansion) becomes one upload named `asset-name` on the product package's GitHub release, tagged with the product's own tag and prerelease flag regardless of the asset owner package's version. An artifact whose `package` is not in the release fails with E179, and a `product-package` that is missing or does not target `github-release` fails with E197. When an artifact's owner package is selected but the product package is not, Callisto warns on stderr, records a `product-artifact-owner-without-product` diagnostic (surfaced in `--format json`; see REL-CMD-04), and derives no slot for that asset.

`release artifact-manifest` requires, for each slot, a regular non-symlink file named `asset-name` directly in `--artifact-dir` (`E221` for a symlink or non-file, an I/O error when missing) and records its sha256 and byte length. With slots, or with a manifest that seals Python or npm files, `release execute` requires both `--artifact-manifest` and `--artifact-dir` (`E233`); otherwise it rejects either flag (`E232`). `--seal-python` records the wheel and sdist of every Python publish of the plan, and `--seal-npm` the one tarball of every npm publish (a registry publish or a platform package, under the published package's own name), each sealed all or none per ecosystem and named for its package and version, and `release execute` verifies each file's sha256 and byte length (`E139`) before any effect.

Before any effect, `release execute` fails with E139 when an artifact's bytes differ from the manifest. It fails with E140 unless `gh attestation verify` passes with the configured `--repo`, `--signer-workflow <repo>/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, `--signer-digest` set to the orchestration revision, `--source-digest` and `--deny-self-hosted-runners`.

In the release workflow, `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` reaches only the `execute` job's execute step. The workflow's default permissions are empty, and the plan and build jobs receive no registry credential.

Callisto finds a GitHub release by tag, draft or published, with the GraphQL `release(tagName:)` lookup followed by `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/{id}`; it never reads the release list. After its own release create, asset upload or publish, a release or asset still absent is looked up again with 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s and 32s waits before the run fails with E167.

`release-pr decide` plans what `version` would apply and returns `noop` when that plan versions no package: no pending changeset names a package and no package with `release-trigger = "auto"` has a bump inferred from commits. A changeset that cannot be parsed fails it with the error `version` reports, so a malformed note never reads as nothing to release. It runs in pre mode too: a changeset an earlier prerelease of the cycle already applied does not count, so a cycle with nothing new is a `noop`, and each merged version commit verifies like any other. It returns `update` when one open PR from the same repository has head `<release-branch>` or `<release-branch>--<40 lowercase hex>`, and `create` otherwise.

`release-pr decide` fails in these cases: an invalid `--repository` flag (E141), an unsafe branch name (E142), duplicate PR numbers (E143), a snapshot for another repository or base branch (E144), a managed-branch PR from a fork (E145), more than one managed PR (E146), a malformed SHA suffix (E147), or a PR headed at `<release-branch>--staging` (E154). Each of these carries its own code even when `--snapshot`/`--decision` is a file, inline JSON, or stdin, except that an invalid repository inside that JSON fails as malformed JSON. A relative file path is read relative to `--cwd`. Malformed JSON fails with E281 (usage, exit 2) when inline or on stdin, and with E238 (runtime, exit 1) naming the file when it is a file; an unreadable file fails with E213. `release-pr verify` accepts either the bare decision wire or unchanged `release-pr decide --format json` output through all three input forms. Report metadata, when present, contains both `command: release-pr decide` and boolean `dryRun`; unknown or duplicate fields and malformed, partial or null metadata fail with E281 (E238 from a file). Nested domain validation retains its typed diagnostic. Verification exits 0 when a fresh snapshot equals the decision's snapshot and fails with E148 otherwise.

`release-pr commit-plan` resolves the repository root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so it works from any subdirectory of the checkout, and emits base64 additions and deletions for the index staged against `--base-commit`. Each added or modified regular file's bytes are hashed without filters and verified against the index blob sha before they are emitted; a worktree file edited again after staging, or whose staged blob differs because a filter changed its bytes, fails the read (E059) rather than emitting content that does not match what is staged. It fails for: no changes (E149); a mode other than 100644, where a symlink or submodule fails before any content is read (E150); a type change or unmerged path (E151); over 4 MiB of content (E152); or a path under `.github/workflows/` or `.git/`, an absolute path, or one containing `..` (E153).

The release-PR action runs the version command with `--emit-decision <decision_path>` (default `.callisto/release-decision.json`) and `--emit-preview <temporary file>`, then composes the PR body with `compose-pr-body --preview --publish-plan` from that file, since the version command has consumed the changesets the body describes. It commits the result with GitHub's `createCommitOnBranch` on `<release-branch>--staging` reset to the base commit, and refuses unless the remote tree equals the locally staged tree. It then moves the release branch ref through the REST API and never runs `git push`. Before creating the commit, before moving the ref, and before any label or PR write, it runs `callisto release-pr verify` against a fresh snapshot and stops when verification fails. After an update ref move is read back successfully, the final check supplies `--applied-head <new_sha>`. This accepts only a consistent update decision's selected PR changing to that exact head; any other snapshot change, wrong applied head, or create/noop use fails E148. The final check is retried up to 9 times, 3 seconds apart, after any verification failure, because the forge can lag a ref move; one that never passes then fails with the last verification's own error, E148 for a head that never shows the applied commit. Checks before the move and the create path retain strict original-snapshot equality.

`callisto-action` with `mode: release` runs `callisto --format json release --receipt <tmp>` and sets `published` and `publishedPackages` from registry and platform publish operations whose outcome is `published`. `mode: execute` runs `callisto release execute` on its `handoff` directory with the same credential mapping and outputs. A `mode` other than `version-pr`, `release` or `execute` fails the step.

With `source: auto`, `callisto-action` and `setup-callisto` default `version` input `latest` installs the callisto release the action's own invocation is pinned to (`github.action_ref` resolved against `orin-dx/callisto`'s `callisto@` tags), falling back to the newest published release only when that ref is unset or matches no tag. A failed tag lookup fails the step. An explicit `version` input overrides this resolution, including inside a Callisto checkout. A consumer manifest mentioning callisto-cli never selects a local build. `source: local` ignores version pins and requires Git-tracked Callisto source at the checkout root plus Cargo metadata confirming the local callisto-cli workspace member, manifest path and callisto binary target. Local builds use explicit manifest and output-directory paths; invalid local source fails without falling back to a downloaded or registry installation.

`--format json` output of `release-pr verify`, `release-pr decide` and `release-pr commit-plan` (without `--out`) goes through the same envelope every other command's JSON report uses: a top-level `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun`, alongside that subcommand's own payload fields unchanged. `release-pr verify --decision` accepts `release-pr decide --format json` output as-is. A failing `release-pr` subcommand's JSON error carries its own `command` (`release-pr verify`, `release-pr decide` or `release-pr commit-plan`) and the `dryRun` flag, as REL-CMD-12 states for the release commands.

The release-PR action retries a forge call that fails with a transient GitHub error (`Something went wrong`, an HTTP 5xx, a gateway or timeout error, a reset or truncated connection) up to 4 attempts, waiting 2, 4 and 8 seconds, and prints a failed attempt's stderr, except for the two probes whose failure is an expected branch (resetting the staging branch and creating a ref that may already exist). A failure of any other kind is not retried. Every call is retried except `gh pr create`, and cleanup of the staging branch. Before each retry of the `createCommitOnBranch` mutation, the staging branch is put back on the base commit. A failed read of the open pull requests, including the one before each verification, stops the action with the failing `gh` call's own error and status.

On every push to `main`, the hold workflow converts each open, non-draft release PR (head `<release-branch>` or `<release-branch>--<anything>` in this repository) to a draft. The release-PR action creates a new PR as a draft and marks a PR ready only after the update or creation succeeded and the base branch still points at the commit the PR was built from; if the branch moved during the run, a ready PR is converted back to a draft and the action warns. A release PR whose refresh failed or never ran therefore stays a draft, and a draft cannot be merged. Hold runs go one at a time, and a newer push replaces a queued run.

`compose-pr-body` renders the release PR body from the same plan as `version`, or from the preview file `version --emit-preview` wrote when given `--preview` (a malformed file or one for another `schemaVersion` fails with E238). With `--publish-plan`, run after `version`, it also plans the release of exactly the packages the preview says are bumped, on the versioned working tree, without observing any registry or the forge (a tagged or moved version is not asked whether it was published), and lists under "Merging will publish" where each package goes (registries, git tag, GitHub release, assets), then one line `Versioned, not published: ` naming, each in backticks, the bumped packages that have no publish target, such as a private fixed-group member, even when nothing publishes (and no line when every bumped package publishes); a plan that refuses leads the body with a caution naming the error instead of the compatibility note. It opens with a package table (highest bump first; the ecosystem comes from the package identity, or from the manifest the bump writes to when the name is bare; the Triggered by column names what triggered the bump, naming up to three changesets and counting more) and a callout: a warning for any major bump, a note that minor bumps below 1.0.0 can break, or a compatibility note. Changes follow under Major, Minor and Patch headings by each change's highest bump. A change shared by several packages appears once and lists them. Each of those headings holds one collapsible block, open for Major and closed otherwise, whose summary reads `<Level>: N change(s)` and whose body lists each change as the changelog renders it, followed by the packages it affects and the pull request that added it. A "Read before merging" callout lists each `Breaking:` and `Action:` marker in a changeset summary with the packages it affects, and the publishable packages whose source (not tests, benches, examples, snapshots or Markdown) changed since their last tag but that no bump or group includes; a breaking marker removes the compatibility claim from the opening callout, a change whose changeset was added by a merged pull request (read from the merge commits with one `git log`, from the merge subject `Merge pull request #N` or a trailing `(#N)`) names it as `#N`, and a `Breaking:` marker on a change whose own bump is below what a breaking change needs (major from 1.0.0, minor before) is listed as "Check the bump" with the packages and the bump it has. The report also lists every label Callisto manages on the release PR with an `applied` flag: `callisto: ready` when nothing below applies, `callisto: blocked`, `callisto: breaking` (a major bump or a `Breaking:` marker), `callisto: action-required`, `callisto: unreleased-changes`, and exactly one of `bump: major`, `bump: minor` and `bump: patch` for the highest bump. The release PR action creates the applied labels that are missing, adds them, and removes the unapplied ones that are on the PR.

A release failure caused by a flag value or flag combination exits 2, and any other failure after the command line is parsed exits 1, each with a diagnostic carrying an `E####` code. clap's own usage error exits 2 with no code.
`--dry-run` with `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release execute`, `release build-python`, `release pack-npm` or `release package-cargo` fails with `E309` and writes nothing.

`[release] targets` with an `asset-name` template expands, in config resolution, to one artifact per target for the product package; `{target}` is the only placeholder. A `[release]` section fails config loading with E197 when it has neither `targets` nor a `[[release.artifact]]`, has only one of `targets` and `asset-name`, uses another placeholder, names a product target also declared by a `[[release.artifact]]`, or has an unsafe `target` or `asset-name`, or a duplicate `asset-name`. An unqualified `product-package` or artifact `package` fails config loading with E317 (a bare name) or E316 (the colon form). A `[release.profiles]` table is an unknown key and fails config loading.
